description: ShipNetSim is an open-source multi-ship simulator for analysing ship energy consumption and emissions in large maritime networks. Built in C++ with Qt6, it combines propulsion and resistance models, real-time environmental data and path finding with visibility graphs and QuadTree indexing to simulate the longitudinal motion of ships of different types, sizes and fuels on real routes; it can test operating strategies such as reduced speed or alternative fuels against IMO standards and model cyber risks such as GPS spoofing and network disruption. It is developed by Ahmed Aredah and Hesham Rakha at the Virginia Tech Transportation Institute and was presented at the 2024 IEEE International Conference on Smart Mobility. It is location independent and runs global or regional networks of sea routes. Installers for Windows and Linux with a GUI (3D globe) and a command-line interface are free on GitHub under GPL-3.0, with documentation; releases reached v0.0.3 and commits continued in June 2026. Caveats: releases are early (0.0.x), the model covers longitudinal motion only, and route and ship inputs must be prepared by the user. ShipNetSim supports network flow, resilience and cascading failure studies of shipping under disruption or cyber attack and energy and emission analysis, and relates to the AIS vessel data and the searoute model catalogued here.
